title: Bellarmine's first escape from idolatry: improper latria when the mind stays fixed on the exemplar alone
source_text: LVII. Quomodo vero imago latria adorari possit, neque tamen in eo committatur crimen idololatriae, variis modis ostendere conantur Scholae Romanae Theologi. Et primo quidem dicit Bellarminus, imaginem quandoque vicem gerere exemplaris, & ea quae fierent circa ipsum exemplar, si adesset praesens, fieri circa imaginem, mente tamen unice defixa in exemplari, non in imagine, & tunc dici posse imaginem coli eodem cultu quo exemplar, non proprie tamen, sed improprie. Sic ex illius mente in die parasceves, seu feria sexta ante Pascha, cum crucifixus paulatim detegitur, & adorandus proponitur, multa quae pertinent ad latriae cultum, circa imaginem crucifixi fiunt; sed omnia illa per imaginem ipsi Christo vero exhiberi intelliguntur: tunc autem proprie loquendo honor ille latriae non defertur imagini, sed soli exemplari: tamen improprie dici potest ipsa etiam imago latria honorari.
pass_a_gloss: But how an image can be adored with latria, and yet the crime of idolatry not be committed therein, the Theologians of the Roman School try to show in various ways. And first indeed Bellarmine says that the image sometimes bears the place of the exemplar, and those things which would be done around the exemplar itself if it were present are done around the image, yet with the mind uniquely fixed on the exemplar, not on the image, and then the image can be said to be cultivated with the same cult as the exemplar, yet not properly, but improperly. Thus according to his mind on the day of Parasceve, or Friday before Easter, when the crucifix is gradually uncovered and set forth to be adored, many things that pertain to the cult of latria are done around the image of the crucified; but all those things are understood to be exhibited through the image to the true Christ himself: then properly speaking that honor of latria is not deferred to the image, but to the exemplar alone: yet improperly it can be said that the image itself also is honored with latria.
pass_b_english: How can image-latria avoid idolatry? Bellarmine's first route: improper latria.
Mind fixed only on the exemplar while Good-Friday crucifix rites use the image as stand-in—latria properly goes to Christ alone, improperly said of the image.

lemmas.gloss: with the mind fixed on the exemplar
